context: activities.likes_count already exists (0 everywhere). New table likes(user_uuid, activity_uuid, created_at) with PRIMARY KEY (user_uuid, activity_uuid) and foreign keys to users/activities.

like.sql / unlike.sql change the likes row AND likes_count in ONE statement (CTEs: me -> inserted/deleted -> bumped). ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes a double like a no-op; GREATEST(...,0) keeps the count >= 0. They return the new count, or NULL when the caller has no users row. Tested 2026-10-03 in PostgreSQL 16: idempotence, 20 concurrent likes by one user -> 1, 20 by different users -> exact, never negative, unknown caller writes nothing.
query_commit returns the first RETURNING column (it detects the uppercase word RETURNING in the CTEs) or None on failure. 0 is a valid count, so ActivityLike tests 'is None'.

home.sql gains liked_by_me for roots and replies via EXISTS on likes joined to users by cognito_user_id = %(cognito_user_id)s. HomeActivities now passes the parameter (None when logged out). The home route switches from claims['username'] to claims['sub'], matching the reply route and what users.cognito_user_id stores.

schema.sql: drop likes FIRST (the old file would fail with 'cannot drop table activities because other objects depend on it' once likes exists; proven in the test), fold the table in, bump the stamp to 17800000000000002. Migration 17800000000000002_create_likes.py creates the table on existing databases (IF NOT EXISTS) and is data/DDL only in migrate_sql(), per the Sept 28 convention.
CORS (Oct 2 lesson): new routes are methods=['POST'] with no 'OPTIONS', so Flask answers preflights. bin/cors-probe gets both routes; C runs it as the acceptance test.

Frontend: ActivityActionLike is overwritten (it was a console.log stub). It POSTs with the same getAccessToken + Bearer pattern as ReplyForm, sends no body, and updates heart/count only from the server's answer. When liked it renders heart-filled.svg (new: heart.svg's outer outline without its cut-out, so same shape and size; heart.svg itself is a ring, so recolouring it would only give a coloured outline). ActivityActionLike.css (new) colours the liked heart and counter in the theme purple rgb(149,0,255) with selectors more specific than ActivityItem.css. ActivityItem passes liked={props.activity.liked_by_me}.
Known limits (by design, not this spec): profile/search feeds don't return liked_by_me, so hearts start unliked there (clicking is still correct: like is idempotent). Logged-out clicks do nothing.
Commits do not deploy. In pilot #4, bin/db/migrate must run right after deploy-all, BEFORE any browser test: home.sql references likes and the feed 500s until the table exists.

create.content:
-- Like an activity: one statement inserts the like (if it is not already
-- there) and bumps activities.likes_count in the same transaction, so the
-- count can never drift from the likes table. Liking twice is a no-op.
-- Returns the activity's likes_count, or NULL when the caller has no users
-- row (the service turns NULL into an error).
WITH me AS (
  SELECT users.uuid
  FROM public.users
  WHERE users.cognito_user_id = %(cognito_user_id)s
  LIMIT 1
),
inserted AS (
  INSERT INTO public.likes (user_uuid, activity_uuid)
  SELECT me.uuid, %(activity_uuid)s::uuid FROM me
  ON CONFLICT (user_uuid, activity_uuid) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING activity_uuid
),
bumped AS (
  UPDATE public.activities
  SET likes_count = COALESCE(likes_count, 0) + 1
  WHERE uuid IN (SELECT activity_uuid FROM inserted)
  RETURNING likes_count
)
SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM me) THEN
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT likes_count FROM bumped),
    (SELECT COALESCE(likes_count, 0) FROM public.activities WHERE uuid = %(activity_uuid)s::uuid)
  )
END AS likes_count

-- Unlike an activity: mirror of like.sql. Deletes the caller's like (if any)
-- and decrements likes_count in the same statement, never below 0.
-- Unliking something you never liked is a no-op.
WITH me AS (
  SELECT users.uuid
  FROM public.users
  WHERE users.cognito_user_id = %(cognito_user_id)s
  LIMIT 1
),
deleted AS (
  DELETE FROM public.likes
  USING me
  WHERE likes.user_uuid = me.uuid
    AND likes.activity_uuid = %(activity_uuid)s::uuid
  RETURNING likes.activity_uuid
),
bumped AS (
  UPDATE public.activities
  SET likes_count = GREATEST(COALESCE(likes_count, 0) - 1, 0)
  WHERE uuid IN (SELECT activity_uuid FROM deleted)
  RETURNING likes_count
)
SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM me) THEN
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT likes_count FROM bumped),
    (SELECT COALESCE(likes_count, 0) FROM public.activities WHERE uuid = %(activity_uuid)s::uuid)
  )
END AS likes_count
